author: kilo-code-bot
body:
**WARNING:** Legacy-synthesis list omits `judge.fallback`, breaking legacy escalation configs it doesn't migrate

The compatibility list maps `judge.baseUrl`/`judge.model`/`judge.apiKeyEnv` → anonymous `systemone` entry and `judge.llm` → anonymous `openai-compat` entry, but the only existing consumer of those fields is the **chain** (packages/judge/src/chain.ts:205-217), where `judge.fallback` names a *connector* resolved via the connector registry. Under the new model `judge.fallback` "names a second provider, not a connector" — an unmodified legacy config has no `providers` entry to resolve that name against, so legacy chain configs either error at startup ("resolves to no entry ... never a silent fallthrough") or silently lose escalation, depending on which rule wins. The synthesis section should pin the legacy behavior: e.g. `judge.fallback: 'llm-judge'` resolves to the synthesized `openai-compat` entry (and `'systemone'` to the synthesized `systemone` entry), so a legacy config's escalation semantics survive the migration release.

---

author: kilo-code-bot
body:
**WARNING:** "Unknown type drops the entry with a warning" conflicts with the adjacent no-silent-misconfig rule

Rules 1 and 2 interact badly: an unknown `type` drops the entry (with a warning), but a consumer referencing that name must "error at use" — while a consumer referencing a *missing* name is "a startup error naming the missing key". So `provider: 'orca'` errors at startup when the entry is absent but only at use-time when the entry exists with a typoed `type` — the same user mistake (`'opena-compat'`) gets two different failure latencies and only the second one mentions the actual cause (the dropped entry), since the error at use can't name the missing key. Consider dropping the entry AND erroring at startup if any consumer reference resolves to a kind-invalid entry, or at least specifying what the use-time error says.

---

author: kilo-code-bot
body:
**SUGGESTION:** `apiKeyEnv` is only mandatory on `systemone`, unlike every legacy judge backend

In the `ProviderEntry` union, `apiKeyEnv` is required only for `systemone`; `openai-compat` (line 84) makes it optional, matching `judge.llm.apiKeyEnv?` (packages/judge/src/config.ts:9). But the existing llm-judge and systemone connectors both reject a missing/invalid env name loudly at decide() time (packages/judge/src/llm-judge.ts:182, packages/judge/src/systemone.ts:138). Worth one sentence on what an `openai-compat` entry with no `apiKeyEnv` does when the judge consumes it — fail at startup, or proceed unauthenticated — so implementers don't have to guess between the two existing precedents.

---

author: kilo-code-bot
body:
**SUGGESTION:** New `BRO_AGENT_PROVIDER`/`BRO_AGENT_MODEL` env names collide with the protected `AGENT_PIN_KEYS` namespace

`spec.env` callers are filtered against `AGENT_PIN_KEYS` (packages/cli/src/agent-connectors.ts:425-433) — `BRO_AGENT_ID`, `BRO_AGENT`, `BRO_SESSION_ID`, etc. — precisely so caller-supplied env can't redirect claims or re-badge a worker. `BRO_AGENT_PROVIDER`/`BRO_AGENT_MODEL` join the `BRO_AGENT*` namespace, so the spec should state that these two ride the protected pin set (connector-owned, filtered from caller `spec.env`) or explicitly remain caller-settable; also note tmux's regex `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` already permits these names, so the only open question is ownership.

---
